A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dense Video Object Captioning work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot, finetuning, tracking-ablation and grounding experiments, including additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on VidSTG and VLN, expanded tracking comparisons, and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.5 excludes the Visual Genome detection loss when training jointly with COCO; v1 Section 3.4 and Table 1 describe using both detection and captioning losses on Visual Genome without this exception. This revises the stated training objective. The architecture, greedy grouping algorithm and hard/soft aggregation procedures otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The same COCO, Aug-COCO, Visual Genome, SMiT, VidSTG and VLN/UVO data support the same captioning and grounding tasks. UVO tracking pretraining and temporally untrimmed VidSTG grounding already appear in v1 Appendix C and remain in v2 Appendix B.

E2.justification: v1 Table 4 compares against a per-frame captioner with an IoU tracker. v2 Table 2 additionally evaluates FairMOT, ByteTrack and a middle-frame-caption/ByteTrack pipeline, substantially expanding the central comparison. The corresponding VLN tracking comparison disappears; grounding comparator membership in Tables 5, 6 and 11 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The default VidSTG configuration changes from soft aggregation to hard aggregation. Table 7's frame-count sweep changes from four-dataset pretraining to Visual Genome pretraining. Numerical CapSwitch evaluation is removed and replaced by categorical caption-consistency indicators, changing how a central property is assessed. VLN Location-QA also stops reporting recall and precision separately.

E4.justification: v2 adds a middle-frame-caption control testing whether enforcing consistency sacrifices caption quality, and analyzes detection and association separately. It removes the VLN tracking ablation and the soft-aggregation comparison from Table 7's frame-count sweep. The disjoint-dataset and UVO-pretraining analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests, including in the appendices.

E6.justification: Captioning results change extensively. Full-model zero-shot CHOTA changes from 28.0/28.2 to 31.1/29.2, and finetuned CHOTA from 54.3/40.8 to 56.9/41.3 on VidSTG/VLN respectively (v1 Tables 2–3; v2 Tables 3–4). Aggregation and pretraining rankings also change. These are revised-setting results, not established same-setting gains. Grounding results in Tables 6 and 11 remain identical.

T1.justification: The formal indicator-based CapSwitch definition in v1 Section 4.1.2 is removed. CHOTA, association and aggregation definitions, and the appendix loss mathematics otherwise remain substantively unchanged. Relocating Algorithm 1 does not introduce a new algorithm or proof.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims a novel tracking algorithm and feature aggregator that ensure temporally consistent captions, strengthening v1's claim of reducing caption switches. The main contributions remain Dense VOC, disjoint supervision and transfer to grounding.

C2.justification: v2 explains the middle-frame baseline's weakness through insufficient temporal context and attributes improvements to association without compromising detection. v1's explanation that Aug-COCO provides no finetuning benefit is dropped. The explicit long-video limitation disappears, while single-caption-per-trajectory and temporal-grounding limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a 0.5 inference proposal-score threshold and changes the promised code release to reported availability, with Appendix A.2 naming chota.py. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.1's padding/truncation to K=16 and association threshold of 0.7 disappear. These are documentation and access-statement changes; external code availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 elaborates its distinction from GTR's post-processing, adds discussion of first-frame-guided single-object tracking/segmentation, and explicitly claims the first generative approach to this grounding task. References add works including ByteTrack, XMem, PaLI-X and Gemini. These refine positioning within the existing research areas.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method explanations are extensively rewritten, including an enumerated contribution list. Tracking analysis precedes disjoint-training results, Algorithm 1 moves into the main method, evaluation subsections are reorganized, and the appendices are reordered.

P2.justification: v2 adds the space–time–language diagram in Figure 2, redraws the model diagram, replaces illustrative clips and restructures the tracking and Location-QA tables. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, and typography, margins, headers and captions are reformatted throughout.

improvement.justification: v2's FairMOT, ByteTrack and middle-frame controls strengthen evaluation of the central end-to-end design beyond v1's IoU-only comparison, and the reorganized presentation clarifies the method. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by lost numerical consistency evidence and tracking hyperparameters. Numerical reporting also develops inconsistencies: v2 Table 4 gives VidSTG CapA 34.5 for row 0, whereas Table 10 gives 35.8.
